grading: structural assertions, not 1-10 scores: every assertion is a checkable property of the response text
baseline: the predecessor ux-craft (diolog-plugins, v1.8.0) run on the identical prompts
notes: E8 is adversarial: it exists so the never-empty-not-checked and no-invented-findings assertions can fail on a surface with no defects, rather than passing vacuously on surfaces that have them.

evals.targets: probe honesty and the no-render branch — the rule that was quarantined behind a model check
evals.prompt: Review the UX of our checkout page. It's at https://staging.internal.invalid/checkout — that host is not reachable from here.
assertions: States plainly that the page could not be rendered or reached, in the report itself rather than only in passing
Does not present findings as though the page had been rendered and inspected
Names which checks were therefore not run, as an explicit and non-empty list
Makes no claim of WCAG conformance or of a passing accessibility check
Either continues from source with the degradation stated, or asks for source — not a fabricated review

evals.targets: the touch-target unit contradiction — three numbers, three standards, one severity call
evals.prompt: Our icon buttons render at 32x32 px with 6px between them. Is that a WCAG failure, and what severity should a review give it?
assertions: States that 32x32 px meets the WCAG 2.2 minimum target size, which is 24x24 CSS px
Attributes the 24x24 figure to SC 2.5.8 at Level AA
Attributes 44 to SC 2.5.5 at Level AAA, or to Apple pt / Android dp, and not to Level AA
Does not report this as a WCAG AA violation or as a Blocker/High accessibility failure
Addresses the spacing question with the criterion's own mechanism (a 24 px diameter circle centred on each target not overlapping another) rather than a flat 8px-gap rule

evals.targets: the state grid as a counted artifact — a categorical enumeration with no count ships as one state
evals.prompt: Mock the runner-pool screen for our CI dashboard. Runners register, claim jobs, go offline.
assertions: Produces an explicit state grid or table before or alongside the screen, rather than only prose about states
Reports a count or fraction of cells built (for example '18 of 18 cells' or '16 of 18, 2 n/a')
Covers at least six named states including loading, empty/first-run, partial, error and done
Marks any inapplicable state as n/a with a stated reason rather than omitting it silently
Describes the loading state against the content it replaces (shape, size, surface) rather than as a generic spinner or grey block

evals.targets: the destructive-action gate table — the second item hoisted out of the model-gated file
evals.prompt: Build the settings screen for our CI runner app. It needs to stop an individual runner, cancel all runners on the host, and restart Docker on the node.
assertions: Tabulates or itemises each destructive action against the specific gate built for it
Refuses a toast as the gate for a host-wide or node-wide action, and says what to use instead
Scales the friction to the blast radius, so the three actions do not all get the same treatment
Does not style or gate the single-idle-runner action as though it were the destructive one
Keeps one primary action in the region rather than placing two equal-weight buttons side by side

evals.targets: the live-region trap and its collision with the skill's own undo-toast recommendation
evals.prompt: Add an 'Archived - Undo' toast to our list view, with a 7 second window, and make sure screen reader users get the announcement.
assertions: Requires the live region to exist empty and permanently in the DOM, with text written into it afterwards
Flags that an interactive element inside a live region is announced as flat text with its role stripped, so an Undo button placed there is not operable
Provides a keyboard-reachable undo outside the live region, or a permanent undo route, rather than only the toast
Notes that a screenshot or static render cannot verify the announcement
Chooses role=status / aria-live=polite rather than assertive for a routine archive confirmation

evals.targets: evidence honesty — the de-rated laws, and the item cap that was wrong in the predecessor
evals.prompt: Should we cut our top navigation from 9 items down to 7? Hick's Law says fewer choices is better, and I've read that people can only hold 7 things in mind.
assertions: Does not endorse a 7-item cap as following from a working-memory limit
Distinguishes a persistent on-screen navigation (recognition, visual search) from something the user must hold in memory (recall)
Qualifies Hick's Law rather than asserting it — either that it applies at decision points, or that it largely fails to transfer to a structured graphical interface
Gives the correct working-memory figure as roughly 4 (3-5) rather than 7, if a figure is given at all
Invents no study, no percentage and no effect size; where evidence is thin, says so

evals.targets: the targeted-edit rule, absent from the predecessor's Build mode
evals.prompt:
Fix the error message on the email field of our signup form. It currently says 'Invalid input'. Here's the form:
Invalid input
assertions: Rewrites the email error to say what happened and how to fix it, with real copy rather than a description
Wires the message to the field (aria-describedby / aria-invalid) as part of that same fix
Leaves the company field's missing label and the vague Submit button unchanged in the code it returns
Raises those other problems as suggestions in the summary rather than applying them unasked
Does not introduce a new colour, component or copy register the surface does not already have

evals.targets: adversarial: a surface with no real defects, so the clean-verdict and not-checked assertions can fail
evals.prompt: Review this component.
assertions: Returns a clean or near-clean verdict rather than manufacturing findings to fill a report
Still states what it could not check, as a non-empty list, despite finding little wrong
Does not claim accessibility conformance from reading the markup
Any finding it does raise is genuine and specific (for example the missing empty/loading/error states, or the placeholder-free label being correct) rather than generic advice
Keeps the report proportional — a short verdict for a small clean component, not a full template with empty sections

evals.prompt: Design onboarding for our time-tracking app. The project ledger already contains a 3-step personalisation wizard. The audience is busy agency owners and the flow must support resume after interruption.
assertions: Names the category-default sequence before choosing the alternative
Chooses one explicit variation axis such as commitment, proof placement, recovery, orientation, or device
Reads the project diversity ledger or reports it absent and records the chosen flow shape after settling it
Includes resume and interrupted-journey recovery because the brief requires it
Does not vary the flow merely for novelty when the user journey or platform convention makes the incumbent shape necessary

evals.prompt: Advise on the structure of a landing page for a B2B report-download campaign. The conversion is one email capture. Do not design a dashboard or multi-step product flow.
assertions: Loads or applies the Persuade conversion reference rather than the product-UI flow reference alone
States one offer, one audience, one primary action, and the conversion event
Places proof beside the claim it supports and handles objections without inventing proof
Keeps the primary action singular and uses an outcome verb
Does not apply the Persuade reference to a dashboard, settings, checkout, auth, or payment surface
